aboutGame.title: What is One Million Coins?
paragraphs: One Million Coins is a short first-person incremental mining game from developer ShoXx, released on Steam on October 13, 2026. You start with empty hands inside an underground vault and a single goal: dig out all 1,000,000 coins, bank them at a deposit station, and spend the proceeds on tools, bags, and skill nodes.

Progression runs on two tracks. Equipment carries you from bare hands to pouches, backpacks, and powered tools that sweep coins in waves, while a 250+ node skill tree spreads upgrades across movement, reach, collection speed, tool strength, capacity, and deposit rate. Restoring bunker infrastructure such as deposit stations, cargo lifts, and conveyors permanently shortens your route, and most players can empty the vault in around two hours.

explore.title: Explore One Million Coins Wiki
explore.description: Eight module hubs cover the whole run: the beginner loop, the 250+ node skill tree, tools and carry capacity, upgrade priorities, vault progression, achievements, PC system requirements, and practical tips.

modules.name: One Million Coins Beginner Guide
modules.description: Learn the core loop, from scooping coins by hand to banking your first haul and buying the pouch that starts your capacity snowball.

highlights.detail: Scoop coins from the pile by hand until you can afford your first upgrade.
Bank at the closest deposit station instead of the far one to save 30 to 40 seconds per trip.
Buy a pouch, then a backpack, so every later trip carries more gold.
Spend your first nodes on collection speed and movement to speed up the whole loop.
Restore the first deposit station you find to turn a long walk into a short one.

modules.name: One Million Coins Skill Tree Guide
modules.description: Plan your points across the 250+ node skill tree, which spreads upgrades over movement, reach, collection speed, tool strength, capacity, and deposit rate.

highlights.label: Capacity
highlights.detail: Raises coins carried per trip and pays off at every stage of the run.

highlights.label: Movement
highlights.detail: Cuts travel time on both legs of the round trip and is the most underrated path.

highlights.label: Collection
highlights.detail: Speeds up how fast each scoop resolves at the coin pile.

highlights.label: Tool Power
highlights.detail: Boosts what each tool action yields before you jump to a new tool tier.

highlights.label: Reach
highlights.detail: Lets you grab coins without repositioning around tall or awkward piles.

highlights.label: Deposit
highlights.detail: Converts banked hauls into spendable funds faster once loads get huge.

modules.name: One Million Coins Tools and Equipment
modules.description: Compare the tool and bag ladder that carries you from bare hands to powered equipment that pulls in waves of coins instead of pinches.

highlights.label: Bare Hands
highlights.detail: Free to use, but tiny scoops mean constant trips back to the deposit station.

highlights.label: Pouch
highlights.detail: Your first real capacity boost and the cheapest quality-of-life jump in the game.

highlights.label: Backpack
highlights.detail: Turns short hops into proper hauls once your first tool unlocks.

highlights.label: Powered Tools
highlights.detail: Coins arrive in scoops rather than pinches and clear piles far faster.

highlights.label: Late-Game Gear
highlights.detail: High-powered equipment sweeps up waves of coins per pass in the final third of the run.

modules.name: One Million Coins Best Upgrades
modules.description: Rank the upgrade paths that matter most so you spend early funds on time saved rather than raw power you cannot carry.

highlights.label: S
highlights.detail: Capacity upgrades: more coins per trip is the hardest early cap and the quiet multiplier behind everything else.

highlights.label: A
highlights.detail: Movement nodes: shorter walks on both legs of the loop compound on every single haul.

highlights.label: B
highlights.detail: Collection speed: pairs with tool strength to clear dense piles near a deposit station.

highlights.label: C
highlights.detail: Deposit rate: worth investing once loads get genuinely huge and banking becomes the bottleneck.

modules.name: One Million Coins Vault Progression Guide
modules.description: Follow the run from the surface pile to the bottom of the bunker, and see which upgrade fixes the bottleneck at each layer.

highlights.detail: Bare hands at the surface: tiny carry size caps your first trips.
First tools speed up scooping close to the entrance.
Pouches and backpacks shift the bottleneck from digging to walking.
Reach nodes recover coins sitting outside your grab range on wider layers.
Restored deposit stations, cargo lifts, and conveyors automate part of the haul.
A full sweep of the deepest layer empties the vault for good.

modules.name: One Million Coins Achievements Guide

highlights.label: Milestones
highlights.detail: Coin total achievements unlock steadily from your very first session.

highlights.label: Efficiency
highlights.detail: Coins-per-minute and per-action feats reward a clean, repeatable loop.

highlights.label: Collection
highlights.detail: Unlocking every item, upgrade, or zone becomes the final bottleneck.

highlights.label: Daily Runs
highlights.detail: Consistency rewards build passively when you return on consecutive days.

highlights.label: Completion
highlights.detail: Endgame mastery feats land last, after everything else is finished.

modules.name: One Million Coins System Requirements
modules.description: Check the minimum and recommended PC specs, from Windows 10 64-bit and 8 GB RAM up to the GPU tier that keeps big coin waves smooth.

highlights.label: Minimum
highlights.detail: Windows 10 64-bit, Intel Core i5-8400 or AMD Ryzen 5 2600, 8 GB RAM, GTX 1060 6 GB or RX 580 8 GB.

highlights.label: Suggested
highlights.detail: Windows 10 or 11 64-bit, Core i7-9700K or Ryzen 5 3600, 16 GB RAM, RTX 2060 or RX 6600.

highlights.label: Storage
highlights.detail: 2 GB of available space for both the minimum and recommended builds.

highlights.label: DirectX
highlights.detail: Version 11 is listed for both spec tiers.

highlights.label: Platform
highlights.detail: Windows only, with Xbox controller support, Steam Cloud saves, and 16 achievements.

modules.name: One Million Coins Tips and Tricks
modules.description: Practical habits for a faster clear: bank every haul, work one dense face, and restore the infrastructure you keep walking past.

highlights.label: Bank Early
highlights.detail: Unbanked coins are dead weight, so deposit whenever a trip is half full.

highlights.label: One Face
highlights.detail: Work a single dense pile in lines instead of chasing scattered coins across the vault.

highlights.label: Bags First
highlights.detail: Buy capacity before raw tool power, because bags pay out on every trip.

highlights.label: Restore
highlights.detail: Deposit stations, lifts, and conveyors permanently shorten your route.

highlights.label: Bank Often
highlights.detail: Hoarding a full load delays every upgrade sitting behind it.

faq.title: One Million Coins FAQ
faq.description: Quick answers to the most common questions about One Million Coins.

items.question: What is One Million Coins?
items.answer: One Million Coins is a short first-person incremental mining game from developer ShoXx, released on Steam on October 13, 2026. You dig 1,000,000 coins out of an underground vault, bank them at deposit stations, and spend the funds on tools and a 250+ node skill tree.

items.question: How long does One Million Coins take to finish?
items.answer: The developer describes One Million Coins as a focused experience most players finish in around two hours. Chasing all 16 achievements usually means a second, more relaxed run because the layout is already familiar.

items.question: Should I buy tools or carry capacity first in One Million Coins?
items.answer: Capacity. Pouches and backpacks pay off on every trip, while tool power only helps while you are scooping, so One Million Coins rewards buying a pouch and a backpack before your first serious tool.

items.question: What should I upgrade first in the One Million Coins skill tree?
items.answer: Start with capacity, movement, and collection speed. One Million Coins spreads its 250+ nodes over seven paths, and specializing in 20-minute blocks beats spreading points evenly.

items.question: Does One Million Coins have a fail state or timer?
items.answer: No. One Million Coins is single-player with no combat, no timer, and no fail state, and it supports saving anytime, so the only resource you are really spending is travel time.
